title: Construction of the cocycle r_{g, F} in (E2)
body_html:
Construction of the cocycle $r_{g, \mathcal{F}}$

Setting: $\mathcal{A}$ a fixed alcove. Define the subcategory $[\mathcal{A}/\mathscr{K}]' \subseteq [\mathcal{A}/\mathscr{K}]$ on facets, with morphisms $$\Hom_{[\mathcal{A}/\mathscr{K}]'}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{E}) = \begin{cases} \hat K_\mathcal{E} & \mathcal{E} \preceq \mathcal{F}, \\ \emptyset & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

A functor $\mathscr{V}' : [\mathcal{A}/\mathscr{K}]' \to R\text{-mod}$ is data $(\mathscr{V}'_\mathcal{F}, r^\mathcal{F}_\mathcal{E})$ of $\hat K_\mathcal{F}$-representations and equivariant restrictions.

Suppose $\mathscr{V}'$ is given with $V_\mathcal{F} := \mathscr{V}'\mathcal{F} \cong \kappa\mathcal{F}$. The goal is to extend $\mathscr{V}'$ to a functor $\mathscr{V} : [\mathcal{A}/\mathscr{K}] \to R\text{-mod}$, which adds the extra data $i_{n, \mathcal{E}} : \mathscr{V}_\mathcal{E} \to {}^{n^{-1}}\mathscr{V}_{n\mathcal{E}}$ for $n \in \Omega := \hat K_{x_0}$.

Constant coefficient system on $\mathbb{I}$

For the barycenter $x_0$ of $\mathcal{A}$, set $$\mathbb{I}_\mathcal{F} := \Hom(V_{x_0}, V_\mathcal{F})_{J_{x_0} \cap J_\mathcal{F}} \;\cong\; (V_{x_0}^* \otimes V_\mathcal{F})_{J_{x_0} \cap J_\mathcal{F}}.$$ Each $\mathbb{I}_\mathcal{F}$ is one-dimensional (by (E4)), and the natural transition maps $r^\mathbb{I}_{\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{E}}$ are isomorphisms, so $\mathbb{I} : [A] \to R\text{-mod}$ is a constant coefficient system.

Cocycle definition

For $k \in \Omega_0$, the transition map sends $1 \in \mathbb{I}_{x_0} \cong R$ to $a_\mathcal{E} := c_\mathcal{E}(1) \in \mathbb{I}_\mathcal{E}$. Define $$r_{k, \mathcal{E}} := ((a_\mathcal{E})^*)^{-1}\,(a_{k\mathcal{E}})_*\,\bigl(\kappa_{x_0}(k)\bigr).$$

Cocycle property

A direct computation (carried out in Sheaf7.tex §8) yields $$(a_\mathcal{E})^*\bigl(r_{k, h\mathcal{E}} \circ r_{h, \mathcal{E}}\bigr) = (a_\mathcal{E})^*(r_{kh, \mathcal{E}}),$$ hence $r_{k, h\mathcal{E}} \circ r_{h, \mathcal{E}} = r_{kh, \mathcal{E}}$.

Combined with the alcove equivalence [𝒜/𝒦] ≃ [A/𝒦] (alcove reduction under (F5)–(F6)), this extends $\kappa$ to a functor on $[\mathcal{A}/\mathscr{K}]$, then to $[A/\mathscr{K}]$, and finally to the full $G$-equivariant coefficient system on $\BSigma$.
